name: River flooding and landslides from atmospheric rivers – south-west BC

geo.extent: Lower Mainland, Fraser Valley, Fraser Canyon and Nicola/Similkameen valleys

description: Autumn atmospheric rivers bring multi-day rain to the coast and southern interior. In November 2021, 200–300 mm fell in 2.5 days in places (Hope ~350 mm in late November); at least 6 people died, close to 15,000 were evacuated, Merritt's 7,000 residents were evacuated, and the Coquihalla and parts of the Trans-Canada Highway were cut.

exposed_areas: Hope and highway corridors to the interior
documented_events: November 2021: 200–300 mm in 2.5 days; ≥6 deaths; ~15,000 evacuations; highways closed into 2022 (ECCC 2021)
2024: atmospheric rivers delivered a double blow to BC (ECCC 2024 list)
practical_implications: Check floodplain maps before buying in the Fraser Valley
Highway links between the coast and interior can close for weeks
Overland flood insurance availability and cost

sources.title: Canada's 10 most impactful weather stories of 2024
Canada's Changing Climate Report (2019) – Headline statements
sources.publisher: Government of Canada (Environment and Climate Change Canada, lead)
sources.methodology: Assessment report; statements are assessments of observed and projected change, not local forecasts

verification.notes: Event facts quoted or paraphrased from the cited official pages on 2026-10-30. Exposure and implications are agent-04 interpretation.

limitations: Fraser River spring freshet risk is not documented in this record (no official page retrieved). Past events show exposure; they are not a prediction for any particular year. Exposure varies street by street – check municipal and provincial hazard maps for a specific property.
